title: Reintroduce compact 'ghost' button variant with focus-rescue and debounce affordances
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Reintroduce a stable compact 'ghost' (borderless) button variant that was regressed during the token namespace migration. The goal is to ship a variant optimized for dense UI surfaces and icon-only usage that: (1) restores keyboard focus and focus-rescue behavior, (2) clarifies loading affordances for icon-only compact buttons (spinner placement and cancelation), (3) standardizes token fallbacks across light/dark/themed modes, and (4) introduces a subtle press-debounce to avoid accidental duplicate activations on touch devices. This ticket owns the design spec, accessibility verification checklist, Storybook examples, and handoff to engineering for runtime constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Visual spec added to Figma with compact dimensions: height 28px, icon size 16px, spacing tokens mapped
Contrast: base and hovered states meet WCAG AA for 3:1 for icon-on-background and 4.5:1 for visible label variants where applicable
Keyboard flow: focus ring appears on Tab and is dismissible only by keyboard blur; focus-rescue behavior restores when a focused button's visible label switches to spinner (icon-only)
Loading: For icon-only compact buttons, spinner overlays the icon (16px spinner) with a transparent touch surface preserved; visible label fallback is present for screen readers
Press-debounce: 250ms debounce applied client-side as recommended, with opt-out token for workflows requiring immediate repeat presses
Storybook: three new stories (compact-ghost/default, compact-ghost/loading-with-cancel, compact-ghost/theming-matrix) with knobs and a11y panel enabled
Regression tests: Percy snapshots added for light/dark/sepia themes and compact density
Engineering handoff: token names documented and migration mapping provided; acceptance PR includes automated accessibility smoke tests
design_notes: Regression root cause: token renaming during token consolidation removed ghost-border opacity fallbacks used in compact mode; we will reintroduce alt tokens rather than re-add legacy names to avoid confusion
Trade-off: Strong focus ring (4px) felt visually heavy in compact contexts; we chose a 2px high-contrast outline with a subtle halo token for low-vision users
Spinner approach: overlay spinner (semi-transparent overlay layer) preferred over icon replacement to preserve hitbox; this keeps visual stability and prevents layout shifts
Press debounce: choose 250ms as balance between preventing accidental double-taps on mobile and not hindering rapid workflows; make opt-out flaggable via token (button.repeat-allow: true/false)
A11y: icon-only must include aria-label and an off-screen text fallback in markup guidelines; add a Storybook accessibility example demonstrating proper labeling
Theming: new tokens introduced: button.compact.ghost.bg, button.compact.ghost.hover, button.compact.ghost.focusRing, button.compact.ghost.spinnerOverlay; each token includes light/dark/brand variants
Docs: add migration guide 'legacy-ghost-to-compact-ghost' describing token mapping and known visual diffs
decisions: Do not resurrect legacy token names; add new compact-scoped tokens and a migration mapping file
Use overlay spinner for icon-only compact buttons rather than swapping content DOM nodes
Adopt 250ms default press debounce with engineering flag to configure per-route
Keep focus ring at 2px with a visible halo for high-contrast themes to minimize layout shift in dense UIs
